svg.aria-label: Animated diagram of incremental WAL compaction. Packs are bottom-aligned squares that grow upward, each labelled with its checksum next to a colored dot. Small packs arrive on the right of the compaction frontier and queue there; with a previous batch already crossed to the left, up to six packs are visible at once — three before the frontier and three after. Every write — each arrival and each compaction — is committed to the object store by a 250ms PUT of gitwal.pb (a tag with an upload progress bar bridging the two boxes) before the next can happen. Once six packs are present, the three after the frontier are compacted into the medium pack; after a few compactions the medium folds into the base pack and a fresh medium grows. The index lists every committed pack with a strictly increasing sequence number and a random checksum.
